articles.headline: Angel Reese wins WNBA defensive player of the year award
articles.standfirst: Angel Reese becomes the first player in Atlanta Dream history to win the Defensive Player of the Year award.
body: Angel Reese of the Atlanta Dream has been named the WNBA's Defensive Player of the Year, marking a historic achievement as the first player in the franchise's history to receive this accolade. The announcement was made on Thursday, with Reese securing 46 of the 74 votes cast by a panel of sportswriters and broadcasters.

In her third season in the league, Reese set multiple records, including the most rebounds in a single season with 500 and the most rebounds in a single game, achieving 26 against the Los Angeles Sparks. She also recorded 32 double-doubles during the season, leading the league with an average of 12.3 rebounds per game, while scoring an average of 16.4 points per game, making her one of only two players to average a double-double this season.

Reese's defensive prowess was evident as the Dream limited opponents to 7.9 points per 100 possessions fewer when she was on the court, the second-best defensive differential among players with significant playing time. Additionally, she ranked third in the league for steals per game, averaging 1.8, and contested 507 field goal attempts, placing her tenth in the league for this statistic.

The Dream's overall defensive performance was strong, ranking third in the league, and Reese's contributions were pivotal in their playoff success, having recently swept the Washington Mystics in the first round. They are set to face the New York Liberty in the semifinals, marking their first appearance in this stage since 2018.
articles.why: Reese's recognition highlights the growing impact of defensive players in women's basketball, which can enhance team performance and attract investment. As the league continues to evolve, individual accolades like this can elevate the profile of women's sports and drive fan engagement.
facts: Angel Reese received 46 out of 74 votes for the Defensive Player of the Year award.
She set a WNBA record with 500 rebounds in a single season.
Reese averaged 12.3 rebounds and 16.4 points per game this season.
The Atlanta Dream's defence ranked third in the league.

articles.headline: Ogunbowale's 45 points propel Wings to game 3 in WNBA playoffs
articles.standfirst: Arike Ogunbowale's record-breaking performance saves the Dallas Wings' playoff hopes.
body: In a crucial Game 2 of the WNBA playoffs, Arike Ogunbowale delivered a historic performance, scoring 45 points to lead the Dallas Wings to a 108-100 overtime victory against the Golden State Valkyries. This achievement not only marked the highest point total in a single playoff game in WNBA history but also allowed the Wings to force a decisive Game 3 in their first-round series.

Ogunbowale's remarkable display included a series of pivotal shots, notably a corner three-pointer that tied the game with just four seconds left in regulation. She opened the overtime period with another three-pointer, contributing significantly to the Wings' scoring in clutch moments, with 13 of the team's 21 points during that critical time. The veteran's performance was vital, especially as her teammate Paige Bueckers struggled, scoring only 10 points on 3-of-13 shooting.

The Wings' victory sets up a winner-takes-all Game 3, scheduled for Friday night in San Francisco. The Valkyries had previously won the series opener convincingly, but the Wings' resilience in Game 2 showcased their determination to advance further in the playoffs. Coach Jose Fernandez highlighted the importance of Ogunbowale's leadership and the contributions from other players like Alysha Clark, who added 21 points off the bench.
articles.why: Ogunbowale's record-setting performance underscores the growing competitiveness and visibility of women's sports. Such high-stakes games attract viewership and investment, crucial for the future of women's leagues.
facts: Ogunbowale's 45 points set a new WNBA playoff record.
The Wings scored 21 points in overtime, with Ogunbowale contributing 13 of those.
Gabby Williams of Golden State scored a career-high 36 points in the same game.

articles.headline: Jordyn Bugg extends contract with Seattle Reign FC until 2030
articles.standfirst: Defender Jordyn Bugg signs a long-term deal with Seattle Reign FC, highlighting her potential.
body: Jordyn Bugg, a defender for the United States women's national team, has signed a new contract with Seattle Reign FC that will keep her at the club until the end of the 2030 NWSL season. This agreement is viewed as a significant long-term investment in Bugg, who has been compared to fellow USWNT defender Naomi Girma, according to Reign general manager Lesle Gallimore.

At just 20 years old, Bugg is in her third professional season and has already earned six caps for the senior national team. Last year, she became the youngest finalist for the NWSL Defender of the Year award, showcasing her rapid development in the league. Bugg expressed her commitment to Seattle, stating that the environment has fostered her growth as a player, allowing her to gain valuable experience on the pitch.

Gallimore noted that while there was external interest in Bugg, the club acted proactively to secure her future. Bugg's versatility as a centre-back, being strong with both feet, adds to her appeal, especially in a position where stability and skill are paramount. Gallimore highlighted Bugg's potential, suggesting that her talent could make her a standout in the league for years to come.
articles.why: This contract extension reflects the growing investment in young talent within women's football, crucial for the league's development. Retaining promising players like Bugg can enhance team performance and attract further sponsorship and fan engagement.
facts: Jordyn Bugg's new contract runs through the 2030 NWSL season.
She has six caps for the senior USWNT and was the youngest finalist for the NWSL Defender of the Year award last year.
Bugg joined Seattle Reign FC in July 2024 after training with the San Diego Wave.

articles.headline: Manchester City and Chelsea face tough challenges in women's Champions League
articles.standfirst: Both Manchester City and Chelsea encounter formidable opponents in the Women's Champions League.
body: Manchester City faced Real Madrid in a highly anticipated Women's Champions League match at the Joie Stadium. The City side, featuring key players such as Beth Mead and Bunny Shaw, aimed to build on their recent success in the Women's Super League, where they ended Chelsea's six-year title streak. City manager Andree Jeglertz expressed confidence in his team's ability to perform despite the ongoing issues affecting the men's team.

Real Madrid arrived with a strong squad, including captain Linda Caicedo, who is known for her ability to influence games. The match was expected to be a tactical battle, particularly in midfield, where City looked to leverage the creativity of Yui Hasegawa and Aoba Fujino against Madrid's robust setup.

In another Champions League fixture, Chelsea played OL Lyonnes to a goalless draw. Despite Chelsea's control of the match, they were unable to convert their chances into goals. Goalkeeper Hannah Hampton made crucial saves to keep the score level, while Chelsea's midfield duo of Keira Walsh and Lexi Potter continued to impress, showcasing their potential on the European stage.

The draw was a testament to Chelsea's defensive resilience against a Lyon side that had been in formidable form, scoring eight goals in their previous league match. Chelsea's performance, particularly given their recent victory over Arsenal, indicates their growing strength in European competition.
articles.why: The outcomes of these matches are significant for the visibility and commercial appeal of women's football. Strong performances from clubs like Manchester City and Chelsea can enhance sponsorship and broadcasting interest in the Women's Champions League.

articles.headline: WTA announces equal prize money for all combined 1000 events by 2027
articles.standfirst: The WTA will implement equal pay for men and women at all combined 1000 events starting in 2027.
body: The Women's Tennis Association (WTA) has confirmed that from 2027, all combined ATP/WTA 1000 events will offer equal prize money for male and female players. This decision marks a significant achievement in the ongoing pursuit of gender equality in tennis, as it aligns with the WTA's commitment initiated in 2023 to ensure equal pay at these prestigious tournaments.

Currently, four of the seven combined 1000 events, including Indian Wells, Miami, Madrid, and Beijing, already provide equal prize money. The Italian Open, Canadian Open, and Cincinnati Open, which previously did not meet this standard, are set to comply by next season. This change comes after years of disparity, exemplified by the 2023 Italian Open, where men received $9.6 million compared to women's $8.3 million.

In addition to the equal pay announcement, the WTA is making structural adjustments to its tournament calendar. The number of mandatory WTA 500 events for top 50 players will decrease from six to four, allowing players greater flexibility in their schedules. This change is in response to player feedback regarding the demands of the tour.

The WTA is also establishing a Tournament Investment Fund aimed at supporting select tournaments financially, particularly in markets where it can have the most significant impact. This initiative is part of a broader strategy to enhance the financial sustainability of the tour amid reported operating losses.
articles.why: This announcement is crucial for the business of women's sport as it sets a precedent for equal pay across high-level competitions. It also reflects the WTA's commitment to financial sustainability and player welfare, which are essential for attracting investment and sponsorship.
facts: All combined WTA 1000 events will offer equal prize money starting in 2027.
In 2023, the men's prize money at the Italian Open was $9.6 million, while women received $8.3 million.
The number of required WTA 500 events for top 50 players will be reduced from six to four.

articles.headline: US set to host inaugural women's Club World Cup in January 2028
articles.standfirst: The United States is likely to host the first Women's Club World Cup, enhancing its role in women's football.
body: The United States is on track to host the inaugural Women's Club World Cup in January 2028, following advanced discussions with FIFA. Los Angeles and San Diego are among the preferred cities for the event, which will feature 19 teams. This tournament will take place shortly after the 2027 Women's World Cup and before the 2028 Olympics, creating a busy schedule for elite players.

FIFA aims to utilise the Club World Cup as a preparatory event for the 2031 Women's World Cup, which the US will co-host with Mexico, Costa Rica, and Jamaica. The organisation is particularly interested in evaluating venues, ticket pricing, and audience demand during this smaller tournament to inform the larger World Cup three years later.

While a formal agreement is yet to be finalised, the US has been cleared to host the tournament without a bidding process, despite Qatar's previous interest. The scheduling of the event in January is designed to avoid conflicts with the men's Copa América, which is set for mid-2028.
articles.why: This development underscores the growing prominence of women's football in the global sports landscape. Hosting such events can significantly enhance investment and commercial opportunities in women's sports.
facts: The Women's Club World Cup is scheduled to start on 5 January 2028.
The tournament will feature 19 teams, following the format of the men's event.
The US is also set to co-host the 2031 Women's World Cup with three other nations.

articles.headline: Decline in female coaches highlights challenges in women's sport
articles.standfirst: A recent study reveals a significant drop in female coaches in the UK, particularly at grassroots levels.
body: The number of female coaches in the UK has seen a notable decline, particularly at grassroots levels, where there has been a 10% decrease in female volunteer coaches. This trend is concerning as it impacts the development pathways for young female athletes in amateur sports. A report from UK Coaching indicates an overall 6% drop in female coaches, suggesting systemic issues that hinder women's participation in coaching roles.

Emily Handyside, a prominent figure at UK Coaching, emphasised that female coaches often feel they must exert greater effort to gain respect and credibility compared to their male counterparts. This perception is reinforced by societal expectations, where coaching is predominantly associated with men. The barriers faced by women in coaching include bullying, harassment, and a lack of equal opportunities, which further complicate their involvement in the sport.

The implications of this decline are significant for young female players. Research from the FA shows that half of all girls involved in organised football feel more comfortable discussing personal matters with a female coach than with a male coach. However, only 7% of grassroots football coaches in England are women, indicating a stark gender imbalance that could affect the development of future talent. Despite progress at elite levels, where the Women's Super League has seen an increase in female managers, grassroots coaching remains a challenge for women.
articles.why: The decline in female coaches limits the growth and representation of women in sports, affecting the development of future talent. Addressing these issues is crucial for fostering an inclusive environment in women's sports.

10% drop in female volunteer coaches at grassroots level.
Only 7% of grassroots football coaches in England are women.

articles.headline: Atlanta Dream and Dallas Wings advance in WNBA playoffs
articles.standfirst: The Atlanta Dream and Dallas Wings secured playoff victories, with Ogunbowale setting a new scoring record.
body: The Atlanta Dream advanced to the semifinals of the WNBA playoffs for the first time since 2018, defeating the Washington Mystics 93-75 in Game 2 of their first-round series. Allisha Gray led the Dream with 22 points, while Jordin Canada contributed significantly with 19 points, 11 assists, and seven rebounds. This victory marked a notable turnaround for the Dream, who had been eliminated in the first round for the past three seasons.

In contrast, the Dallas Wings faced a more dramatic situation in their playoff series against the Golden State Valkyries. Arike Ogunbowale delivered a record-breaking performance, scoring 45 points in a thrilling 108-100 overtime victory in Game 2. This achievement set a new WNBA playoff record for points scored in a single game, surpassing the previous record of 42 points.

Ogunbowale's performance was crucial as it not only kept the Wings' playoff hopes alive but also showcased her resilience after a challenging season. The team will now prepare for a decisive Game 3 in San Francisco, where they aim to advance further in the playoffs. This game is particularly significant as it represents the first time Golden State has reached the playoffs in its second season.
articles.why: The advancements of the Dream and Wings highlight the growing competitiveness of the WNBA, which can attract more investment. Ogunbowale's record-setting performance may enhance individual player marketability and league visibility.
facts: Atlanta Dream advanced to the semifinals for the first time since 2018.
Arike Ogunbowale scored 45 points, a new WNBA playoff record.
This is the first time Golden State has reached the playoffs in its second season.

articles.headline: New York Liberty make WNBA history by upsetting Minnesota Lynx
articles.standfirst: The New York Liberty become the first No 8 seed to eliminate a No 1 seed in WNBA history.
body: In a historic upset, the New York Liberty defeated the Minnesota Lynx 87-71, marking the first time a No 8 seed has eliminated a No 1 seed in the WNBA's 30-year history. Jonquel Jones and Breanna Stewart each scored 21 points, while Sabrina Ionescu contributed 18 points, leading the Liberty to a two-game sweep in the first round of the playoffs.

The Liberty's victory was characterised by their strong start, taking an early lead and maintaining control throughout the game. They finished the first half with a 49-37 advantage, and despite the Lynx's attempts to close the gap, New York's size and defensive capabilities proved too much for Minnesota to handle.

The Lynx, who had the best regular-season record at 33-11, struggled offensively, shooting only 38.2% from the field. Rookie of the Year Olivia Miles had a particularly challenging game, scoring just five points on 1 of 8 shooting and was benched for much of the second half after a flagrant foul on Stewart. This disappointing end to the season follows the Lynx's previous playoff exit, raising questions about their performance under pressure.
articles.why: This historic upset highlights the increasing competitiveness of the WNBA, which can attract greater investment and viewership. It also underscores the importance of playoff performance, which can significantly impact team valuations and sponsorship opportunities.
facts: New York Liberty are the first No 8 seed to defeat a No 1 seed in WNBA history.
The Liberty's victory came in a two-game sweep of the Lynx in the first round of the playoffs.
The Lynx finished the regular season with a record of 33-11, the best in the league.

articles.headline: Katy Marchant retires from elite cycling after successful career
articles.standfirst: Olympic gold medallist Katy Marchant announces her retirement from competitive cycling.
body: Katy Marchant, the 33-year-old Olympic gold medallist, has confirmed her retirement from elite cycling. Marchant's decision comes after a successful career that culminated in a gold medal in the women's team sprint at the 2024 Paris Games, alongside teammates Emma Finucane and Sophie Capewell. In addition to her Olympic success, she also secured world and European titles in the same year.

Reflecting on her career, Marchant expressed pride in her achievements, stating, 'I’ve achieved more than I could ever have dreamed of achieving.' Although she had previously aimed to compete in the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, she ultimately decided against extending her career, citing the physical and mental demands required to continue at an elite level.

Marchant's journey in cycling included significant personal milestones, as she returned to competition after the birth of her first son, Arthur, and more recently, her second son, Walter. She was the first female track sprinter in Great Britain to return to elite racing after becoming a mother, setting a precedent for other athletes in similar situations.

Throughout her career, Marchant has been a pivotal figure in women's sprint cycling, often competing alone in major events and nurturing younger teammates. She expressed a mix of sadness and pride about stepping away, acknowledging her role in fostering a supportive environment for future cyclists.
articles.why: Katy Marchant's retirement marks the end of a significant era in women's sprint cycling. Her achievements and advocacy for mothers in sport highlight the evolving landscape of female athletics.
facts: Marchant won gold in the women's team sprint at the 2024 Paris Olympics.
She has two Olympic medals: gold in 2024 and bronze in 2016.
Marchant returned to competition six months after the birth of her second child.
